Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 5f773519639041faed4132f5943d7895f9078a4c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Maciej Machnikowski <maciej.machnikowski@intel.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2021 09:50:18 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] ice: Fix perout start time rounding

Internal tests found out that the latest code doesn't bring up 1PPS out
as expected. As a result of incorrect define used to round the time up
the time was round down to the past second boundary.

Fix define used for rounding to properly round up to the next Top of
second in ice_ptp_cfg_clkout to fix it.

Fixes: 172db5f91d5f ("ice: add support for auxiliary input/output pins")
Signed-off-by: Maciej Machnikowski <maciej.machnikowski@intel.com>
Tested-by: Sunitha Mekala <sunithax.d.mekala@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Tony Nguyen <anthony.l.nguyen@intel.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210813165018.2196013-1-anthony.l.nguyen@intel.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_ptp.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_ptp.c
index 5d5207b56ca9..9e3ddb9b8b51 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_ptp.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_ptp.c
@@ -656,7 +656,7 @@ static int ice_ptp_cfg_clkout(struct ice_pf *pf, unsigned int chan,
 	 * maintaining phase
 	 */
 	if (start_time < current_time)
-		start_time = div64_u64(current_time + NSEC_PER_MSEC - 1,
+		start_time = div64_u64(current_time + NSEC_PER_SEC - 1,
 				       NSEC_PER_SEC) * NSEC_PER_SEC + phase;
 
 	start_time -= E810_OUT_PROP_DELAY_NS;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_ptp.c`**
   - The line that calculates `start_time` when it is less than `current_time` has been modified. 
   - The original code used `NSEC_PER_MSEC - 1` for rounding, which caused the time to round down to the past second boundary.
   - The updated code now uses `NSEC_PER_SEC - 1`, which correctly rounds up to the next top of the second.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `ice_ptp.c` addresses a bug identified in the previous implementation that was introduced in commit `172db5f91d5f`. The bug caused the 1PPS (One Pulse Per Second) signal to not function as expected due to incorrect rounding of the start time. By changing the rounding definition, the patch ensures that the start time is correctly set to the next second boundary, thereby fixing the issue with the 1PPS output.

1. analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 
2. output the file name that is most likely to cause the bug.

Reason:
The use of `NSEC_PER_MSEC - 1` incorrectly rounds the `start_time` down to the past second boundary instead of rounding it up to the next top of the second. This results in the 1PPS output not functioning as expected.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
start_time = div64_u64(current_time + NSEC_PER_SEC - 1,
```
Reason:
By changing the define to `NSEC_PER_SEC - 1`, the code now correctly rounds the `start_time` up to the next top of the second, ensuring that the 1PPS output operates as intended.
